citation.authors: Wolever TMS, Jenkins AL, Campbell JE, Ezatagha A, Dhillon S, Johnson J, Schuette J, Chen Y, Chu Y
citation.title: Decreasing the RAG:SAG ratio of granola cereal predictably reduces postprandial glucose and insulin responses: a report of four randomised trials in healthy adults

population.description: Granola studies 1-3, 120 completers (n 40 each; Table 2 'Total (n 120)': 67 male, 53 female; age 35.2 +/- 13.9 and BMI 24.8 +/- 2.8, means with SD as printed, min and max not printed). Males and non-pregnant females aged 18-65 with BMI 21.0 to <32.0 kg/m2 and fasting serum glucose <7.0 mmol/l (no glucose tolerance test); the paper's title calls them healthy adults, but only fasting glucose was screened (no glucose tolerance test) and 41% had BMI >= 25 (Table 2) with enrolment up to BMI <32, so the status is unselected (README). Each study's age and BMI are a protocol override. The pilot (n 40) is also an override; its fasting insulin is the only pilot value entered.

protocols.name: cg1_meal
protocols.description: Control granola 1 (CG1, study 1, n 40) with 122.5 g skim milk, eaten within 10 min from the first bite; first bite at arm minute 10 (the paper's 0 min). Fasted: a 10-12 h overnight fast with water allowed (prefast_hours 10 is the lower end of the printed range, assumed). Meal entered as two items at minute 10, each as printed in Table 1 (not summed): granola 54.3 g (Table 1, CG1 row: protein 4.9 g, fat 5.2 g, avail carbohydrate 32.9 g, fibre 4.7 g) and skim milk 122.5 g (Table 1: protein 4.1 g, fat 0.1 g, avail carbohydrate 6.1 g, fibre 0.0 g). Two fasting samples 5 min apart (-5 and 0 min) are arm minutes 5 and 10, so the fasting baseline is the mean over minutes 5-10 (baseline_window 5-11, end exclusive). Blood glucose (finger-prick, fluoro-oxalate tube) and serum insulin at 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105, 120, 150 and 180 min after the first bite are arm minutes 25, 40, 55, 70, 85, 100, 115, 130, 160 and 190. Duration 191 min.

protocols.name: fasting_pilot
protocols.description: Fasted morning of the pilot (chew) study test day, no food: 10-12 h overnight fast with water allowed (prefast_hours 10 is the lower end, assumed). The paper's fasting value is the mean of two samples 5 min apart (-5 and 0 min), placed at arm minutes 5 and 10; duration 11 min (minutes 0-10) is our run-in, not stated by the paper. Table 2 does not say which visit(s) its fasting values come from; the paper's HOMA uses four fasting measures across two test meals, so the printed value may be a mean over two mornings.

Pilot chews C1-C6 (Table 3): glucose and insulin iAUC 0-2, 2-3 and 0-3 h and the 2 h glucose increments; six starch variants at 35 g available carbohydrate, with a drink of the subject's choice whose grams are not printed
Pilot fasting glucose (Table 2: 4·48 ± 0·39 mmol/l; Results text, cited to Table 2: 4·36 ± 0·49 mmol/l) and the six chew-day fasting means (4.45 to 4.53 mmol/l, sem): the printed values disagree

Table 4 iAUC 0-3 h, glucose and insulin, CG1, CG2 and CG3 (and the pilot chews): each is the 0-2 h area plus the 2-3 h area, both entered, from the same samples of the same people (glucose 118+10=128, 118+10=128, 119+6=125; insulin 147+12=159, 201+12=213, 205+13=218, all as printed)
Table 4 'Mean of three studies' control column: glucose and insulin iAUC and 2 h increment pooled over the three control meals, whose grams differ; n for its sem not printed
Table 2 'Total (n 120)' fasting glucose and insulin: pooled over the three granola studies
Glucose and insulin increments at each sampling time, pooled and by study (Figure 2 A-F, means +/- sem): figure only, so the curve to 180 min is not printed as numbers
Relative glycaemic and insulinaemic responses (test as a percentage of control, per person, outliers more than 2 sd removed, and their means and 99% or 95% CIs; Results, Fig 2 insets, Fig 3)
HOMA-IR, HOMA-B and the share with HOMA-IR >= 1 (Table 2)
